answer:
At 700 bar and 25 °C, hydrogen has a density of about **39.2 kg/m³**.

I computed this with CoolProp 6.x, which uses the Leachman et al. (2009) equation of state for hydrogen:
- Normal hydrogen: ρ = 39.22 kg/m³, compressibility factor Z = 1.451.
- Para- and ortho-hydrogen give the same value to within 0.01 kg/m³ (39.217 and 39.218 kg/m³).

As a consistency check, the ideal-gas density is P/(RT) = 70×10⁶ / (4124.2 × 298.15) ≈ 56.9 kg/m³. Dividing that by Z = 1.451 gives 39.2 kg/m³, so the two numbers agree.

Because Z is about 1.45, the ideal-gas law would overestimate the density by about 45% at this pressure, so a real-gas equation of state is needed.

I did not compare the result against NIST REFPROP or Webbook tables. No files were created.
